usb_capture_limit: ends ~t=41s, before the 42.4s fault; data recovered from the persistent logdump instead

cp_stall_probe.cp_ahb_fault: 0x0903a284 (bit31 error=0; stale residue, not an active fault)

finding_that_refines_the_model: At the FIRST UCHE out-of-bounds interrupt (t=42.613 s) the ring read and write pointers are EQUAL (rptr=wptr=0xb1). The CP had already drained the ring; it is NOT stalled mid-fetch and NOT waiting on a memory barrier. This corrects the earlier 'CP stopped fetching mid-ring' reading, which came from a later snapshot sample (rptr 0xc0 vs wptr 0x107) taken at fault-check time, not at the interrupt.

confirmed_unchanged.smmu: sctlr=0 translating=0 far=0 fsynr=0 (bypassed at draw time)

root_cause_chain: 1. VSC binning pass issues a UCHE access to the 4 KiB VSC size buffer
2. UCHE rejects it (OOB) although gpu/dma/page_to_phys all agree and the SMMU is bypassed
3. VSC produces no visibility output (size buffer all zero, VSC_PIPE_DATA_ADDRESS reads 0, VSC_BUSY clear)
4. CP drains the ring with no error latched
5. Hang detector fires ~60 ms later; GPU wedged; SurfaceFlinger never renders
open_question: step 2 only: why the UCHE rejects an access whose buffer is proven physically valid. All buffer-identity and aperture-register hypotheses are eliminated.
